title: [PM-41691] Fix issue where edit item, hidden passwords wipes password, TOTP
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-41691

## 📔 Objective

Fixes bug QA found where edit item, hidden passwords would then wipe password and TOTP fields

inline.body:
❓ **QUESTION**: The restore is unconditional, so an explicitly supplied password/TOTP is silently discarded rather than rejected — is that the intended behavior?

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The comment above describes handling round-tripped redacted `null`s, but this also overwrites non-null values the caller deliberately set. A user with edit-but-not-view permission who submits `login.password: "new-value"` (e.g. a rotation script) gets `success` back with the old password still stored and no indication the change was dropped.

Guarding on the redacted marker keeps the previous behavior for explicit writes while still fixing the bug:

```ts
if (cipherView.login.password == null) {
  cipherView.login.password = originalLoginPassword;
}
```

If the intent is instead to match the web/browser clients, which disable these inputs entirely for `viewPassword === false`, returning `Response.badRequest(...)` when a non-null value is supplied would make the rejection visible instead of silent.

</details>

comments.body:
## 🤖 Bitwarden Claude Code Review

**Overall Assessment:** APPROVE

Re-reviewed the CLI `edit item` fix that preserves login password, TOTP, and hidden custom field values when a user without `viewPassword` permission round-trips a redacted item back through `bw edit`. The write path now correctly mirrors the existing redaction in `apps/cli/src/vault/models/cipher.response.ts` and `login.response.ts` (PM-16160 / PM-33526), and no decrypted data is logged or returned to a caller that could not already see it. Both findings from the previous review are resolved: hidden field values are now keyed by field name with FIFO ordering for duplicate names instead of by array position, and password/TOTP/hidden restores are guarded on a `null` value so an explicitly supplied value is a deliberate write and is left alone. Test coverage exercises the redacted round trip, the remove-and-reorder case, and the explicit-write case.

<details>
<summary>Code Review Details</summary>

No findings.

Verified during this pass:

- `CipherExport.toView` leaves `view.login` and `view.fields` untouched when `req.login` / `req.fields` are omitted, so the restore block is a no-op on partial requests.
- `CipherView.viewPassword` defaults to `true`, so users with view permission are unaffected by the new block.
- `passwordHistory` is redacted to `undefined` in the response and is therefore retained from the decrypted view on round trip — no additional handling needed.

</details>
